To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Synthetic data can be used to train deep neural network word recognisers.

(i) we have a new framework for text recognition that is simple and fast, and that does not require any labelled data for training; (ii) we can use synthetic data to train our text recognition models; (iii) we can use the synthetic data to train a neural network that can be used as a text generation engine, and this engine is capable of producing synthetic data that is realistic and sufficient for training text recognition models; and (iv) we have three new word recognition models,

(1) synthetic data, produced by an image generation engine, is sufficient to train a deep neural network to recognize text in images, (2) the deep neural network can be trained to recognize text without any real data, and (3) the deep neural net can recognize words in a variety of different ways, including via a dictionary, via character sequences, and via n-gram sequences
In summary, our research is concerned with
three aspects of the problem of text recognition in natural scene images: 1) synthetic data generation, 2) deep learning models, 3) text recognition in natural images.

three main contributions: 1) the use of artificial neural networks for the task of natural scene text recognition; 2) the use of synthetic text data in the training of these neural networks; 3) the use of a holistic approach to word recognition, as opposed to a character-based approach.

the following questions: Can we train a word recognizer on a synthetic text dataset? How does the performance of our models compare to other methods? How does the size and complexity of the models affect the recognition performance? Can we train a single model that is able to recognize text in different languages and scripts?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a framework for the holistic recognition of unconstrained text that is fast, accurate and does not require any real data, and we believe that this is a significant contribution to the field of scene text recognition.
our framework has achieved a new state-of-the-art on the standard datasets, with a very simple, fast, and efficient architecture.
we have shown that synthetic data can be used to train neural networks that perform word recognition on natural images, and that these networks can be trained to out-perform the state-of-the-art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a framework that can be trained on synthetic data and can perform word recognition on the entire image holistically.
, in the context of text recognition, synthetic data and deep neural networks can be a powerful combination.

we show the possibility of using synthetic data to train a neural network for natural scene text recognition, and that we can achieve state-of-the-art results on the ICDAR 2013 Robust Reading Competition and the ICDAR2013 Incidental Scene Text dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can achieve state-of-the-art text recognition accuracy without any real data at all, and that we can do so using very simple and fast models.

we can use the synthetic data to learn to recognise natural scene text, and that the neural network models can be used to recognise words from natural scene images without the use of character models.

the combination of synthetic data and deep neural network architectures can lead to a new paradigm in text recognition, one that can scale to any size, language or application, and one that is highly cost-efficient and flexible.
